subject: Ownership lacuna: resync and revised MAP

Subject: Proposed MAP and timeline — readiness question

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. We tried to map your recommended acceptance gates into our internal schedule and ran into a sequencing problem: our security signoff (internal) is not owned by the same group that will own the acceptance test environment, which creates a handoff gap that pushes our acceptance window out by ~3 weeks.

Attached is the MAP v3 with annotations (highlighted rows). The ask: can Redwood commit to a staged cutover that allows a soft-launch for a subset of tenants while procurement and final SOW negotiations finish? Procurement is also asking for a performance SLA clause tied to the soft-launch.

Short answers appreciated — we are trying to firm a go/no-go by next Thursday (Jun 3).

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Nexigen Health

Daniel — thanks for the note and the annotated MAP.

Quick read: the handoff you describe is the root cause of the 3-week shift. We can support a staged cutover (soft-launch) but need clarified ownership and an explicit fallback plan if the security group delays validation. Proposed path:
- Redwood provides a tenant-scoped soft-launch config for up to 10 pilot tenants (no shared data paths).
- Redwood guarantees incident response SLAs for the pilot (24x7 P1) during the pilot window.
- Procurement SLA language can be templated; legal would need a 48-72 hour review for redlines.

I propose a short working session today with Ben (CS lead on onboarding) and Jonas (solutions lead) to lock the cutover mechanics and draft the temporary SLA language for procurement. If we can align, we can keep the go/no-go on Jun 3.

Available windows: 11:30–12:15 or 15:00–15:45 PT. Which works?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Escalation: request for exec acceptance on pilot fallback SLA (Nexigen DX-4782)

Soojin — looping you in. Nexigen's security/procurement split has created an ownership lacuna that threatens the Jun 3 go/no-go. We have a concrete mitigation (staged pilot + documented fallback SLA) but procurement insists on an exec-level acceptance if we cut over before security validation. They asked who at Redwood can sign off.

Context: Ben can operate the pilot environment and Jonas will run integration validation. Procurement wants the acceptance inline in the SOW; they will not sign without an exec signoff name. If we provide an exec-level named acceptance (not necessarily a legal guarantee beyond the SOW fallback language), it materially improves the probability of keeping the close date.

Suggested options:
1) Provide a named acceptance from Sales leadership (you) with explicit timeboxed remediation commitments and an internal risk log.
2) Offer a commercial concession (one-month credit) in exchange for procurement signing the staged SOW now and committing to finalize security validation within 30 days.

Recommendation: Option 1 + limited credit (option 2) only if procurement refuses. This preserves commercial integrity while buying runway. Need guidance by EOD on June 1 to prep the SOW.

Attachment: escalation-onepager.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Grace

— Soojin
